rationale: This is a cosmetic re-weighting of the archived "Growth Cash Maturity Match" (RANK→INDICATOR on the same growth gate with an identical cash-margin-minus-current-debt spread), and the indicator additionally destroys information by collapsing all non-growers to exactly zero, which lands them in the middle of the spread's [-1,1] range rather than excluding them.

The construction is coherent, but TS_SUM(xrd,5)/at is close to a 5x-scaled smoothing of xrd/at for the persistent R&D spenders that dominate the long leg, so its cross-sectional rank will be very highly correlated with the archived "Intangible Cash Maturity Shield" (fmb 5.25, ls_talpha 4.64) — this is a robustness check on the best existing signal, not a new mechanism.

Internally consistent and correctly signed, but it is a component swap within an already-explored family — identical to "Current Debt R&D Cost Shock" with the R&D-cut leg replaced by a margin-decline leg, and overlapping "Current Debt Gross Margin Squeeze" — so it adds little beyond confirming that current-debt concentration times deteriorating fundamentals is negative.

This is a mechanical crossover of two archived signals — the rollover scaler MIN(dltis,dltr)/at from "Rollover Cash Coverage Strain" bolted onto the exact MIN(NEG(ΔR&D intensity), Δxint/lt) conditioning block from "Current Debt R&D Cost Shock" — with no new economic content, and the WINSOR'd raw scaler times a bounded rank product will be driven mostly by a handful of large refinancers.

This is a direct rediscovery of the archived "Externally Funded SG&A Productivity Gap" with the spread negated and the expected sign flipped (and financing narrowed to dltis only), which is the same signal up to sign and already tested weakly (fmb -0.76, ls_talpha 0.72); the hypothesis also says growth "follows" issuance while the expression is contemporaneous with no LAG.

This is the sign-flipped archived "Dilutive Buyback Cash Gap" with sstk/at bolted on, and the bolt-on is badly constructed — ADD(GROWTH(csho,1), RATIO(sstk,at)) sums two unranked, differently scaled quantities before ranking, so whichever has larger raw dispersion (typically the csho growth tail) silently dominates the dilution leg.
